_doc: The REGISTRY of what render-shelf.md's Part 2 declares — id, name, kind. Beside
render-tokens.json (the numbers) and render-lab.json (the lab). A registry is not numbers,
which is why it is its own file rather than a key in the tokens.
It exists because Part 2's numbering is INVENTION ORDER, not identity: V14 sits between V11
and V12 in the file, and the twenty-one headings hold at least five different KINDS of thing
under one sequence. A catalog state that says `drawn_by: ["V9"]` would be naming a mechanism
— how a secret reaches a pixel — not something a reader can see. So the kinds are named here
primitive  — a drawing element cap builds. A state may cite it in `drawn_by`.
mechanism  — HOW a secret reaches a pixel. A primitive is built on one; nothing draws it.
platform   — Blizzard draws it and cap leaves it alone.
retired    — gone. Kept so a citation to it fails loudly rather than resolving to silence.
The ids are stable and cited across every spec doc — they are never renumbered, and a
retired entry keeps its slot forever. `capart check` gates this file against Part 2's
headings in both directions, name included.
⚠ V5.1 (the cue vocabulary) is deliberately NOT here. It is a vocabulary, not a thing that
draws; V5 is the primitive that draws every member of it. It stays prose in Part 2.
